Title: Scope and permissions
Given: A clean implementation checkout and the baseline
When: Review the release scope and call each privileged route as visitor, volunteer and operator
Then: Only the role matrix grants access; no deferred capability is presented as delivered; generated contracts implement this baseline
Verification: Document review and API authorization matrix

Title: Domain boundaries
Given: Records with every enum and Unicode boundary fixture
When: Create with valid values, at limit and one beyond; submit client status/date; read publicly
Then: Valid records persist with server AVAILABLE/UTC; invalid fields reject with 400; code-point counts match UI; no private fields appear
Verification: DTO validation, API and mapper tests

Title: Stale updates and deletion
Given: Two staff clients share an ETag and a separate stone has an active hold
When: Save from both clients; omit If-Match; attempt deletion of held and free stones
Then: First save succeeds, stale requests return 412, missing preconditions return 428, active hold returns 409; valid delete hides the stone and preserves tombstone/cleanup intent
Verification: PostgreSQL concurrent integration test

Title: Routes and return state
Given: A filtered paginated catalog is scrolled down
When: Open a detail, use Back/Forward and Back to catalog; refresh canonical/legacy/unknown routes
Then: Session catalog state restores; direct/reload defaults apply; canonical redirects replace history; missing record and unknown route are distinct
Verification: Playwright API-mode navigation

Title: Filtering and counts
Given: A fixed catalog contains available/reserved/adopted stones across types, sizes and UTC day boundaries
When: Apply two sizes, two types and From/To; sort all six ways; paginate; request non-AVAILABLE status
Then: OR/AND/half-open UTC rules, AVAILABLE invariant, exact total, deterministic ties and page bounds hold; no wrong-status card leaks
Verification: Repository/API parameterized tests

Title: Draft filters and chips
Given: Applied valid dates and several selected options exist
When: Type an invalid date, filter option labels, remove hidden selections/date chip and Reset
Then: Invalid draft never replaces applied date; query does not search catalog; chips/counts share state; reset and focus behavior match requirements
Verification: UI interaction tests and keyboard browser charter

Title: Responsive layout and focus
Given: Catalog/detail with chat open and filters/adoption modal available
When: Exercise 320, 768 and 1440 px widths, 200% zoom, keyboard navigation and Escape and reduced motion
Then: No horizontal overflow or hidden focus; modal traps only when appropriate; chat respects inert background; cards and controls remain readable
Verification: Playwright plus screen-reader inspection

Title: Loading errors and gallery
Given: Zero/one/many-photo stones and controlled response delays
When: Load/retry failure, return successful empty result, select thumbnails, break an image and reverse request completion order
Then: States differ correctly; newest query wins; no fabricated thumbnails/retry loop; preview never changes cover; full biography remains readable
Verification: Component tests and real browser checks

Title: Upload validation and ownership
Given: Authorized staff plus a foreign staff session and visitors
When: Upload supported files at 10 MiB and over, MIME/signature mismatch, corrupt/animated/oversized-pixel files and metadata-bearing image
Then: Only valid bounded decoded images accepted; metadata removed; private keys hidden; foreign draft returns 404; unauthorized upload returns 401/403
Verification: File-security integration fixtures and authorization tests

Title: Atomic create and lost response
Given: Sixteen owned drafts and two concurrent creators
When: Create at expiry boundary, reuse/duplicate references, race claims and drop the successful HTTP response
Then: One atomic winner; expired/duplicate/foreign cases fail without partial stone; same-key replay gives original result; changed payload returns 409; valid drafts survive confirmed rollback
Verification: Database race, clock and fault-injection tests

Title: Photo repair and cleanup
Given: A new stone has one failed permanent copy and retained source
When: Restart worker through retry schedule, repair storage, exhaust a second photo, manually retry and remove a pending photo
Then: Saved stone survives; states/retry count persist; ready URL appears only after copy; cleanup never deletes an attached sole copy and eventually removes detached bytes
Verification: Isolated MinIO integration with controlled clock

Title: Usable create workflow
Given: Staff opens an empty form
When: Select mixed valid/invalid batches, reorder, remove cover, fail one upload, retry creation and choose Add another
Then: Progressive previews/counts/order are correct; successful drafts retained; fields/errors/focus preserved; no duplicate POST; confirmation and fresh form work
Verification: Playwright real API with isolated uploads

Title: URL expiry and contracts
Given: READY and PENDING photos with controllable signed-link expiry
When: Read detail/draft, expire URL and refresh; inspect serialized representations
Then: Only READY has a URL; refresh bounded once; no permanent signed URL storage; response fields/enums/nullability conform to generated schema
Verification: API contract tests and browser expiry case

Title: Application submission
Given: An AVAILABLE stone and two independent visitor sessions
When: Open modal, test empty/Unicode limits, submit concurrently and fail a post-success refresh
Then: Exactly one 201/PENDING/RESERVED result and one 409; success retained on refresh error; modal shows correct stone and expiry; no PII public leak
Verification: PostgreSQL race plus Playwright application charter

Title: Lifecycle and expiry boundary
Given: PENDING application before its 72-hour boundary, with a fixed UTC clock
When: Extend once, extend twice, complete before expiry, race cancel/complete, then apply at/after expiry on another stone
Then: One extension only; one compatible terminal transition; due hold becomes EXPIRED and AVAILABLE atomically; effective reads/search agree; new application can follow a cancelled/expired one
Verification: Clock-controlled repository/service/API tests

Title: Staff queue privacy and abuse
Given: Pending/terminal applications with synthetic contacts
When: Use queue filters/actions; cross role boundaries; hit session/IP limits; advance retention clock
Then: Authorized private queue works; visitor cannot read contacts; 429 includes truthful delay; protection outage returns 503; terminal PII purged at 30 days and minimal audit removed at 90 days
Verification: Staff browser charter, authorization and retention tests

Title: Write uncertainty and replay window
Given: Saved create/application/reindex outcomes and retained key markers
When: Retry identical/changed payloads before 72 hours and after 72 hours; simulate lost commit acknowledgement
Then: Original result replays without new work; changed/expired-used keys return 409; uncertainty reconciled before a new mutation; no assumed rollback
Verification: Transactional idempotency fault tests

Title: Chat lifecycle and ownership
Given: Two browser sessions and an owned conversation with saved turns
When: Send Unicode/IME input, navigate/collapse pending work, reload, access a foreign UUID and advance TTL
Then: One pair per turn; original context retained; reload restores saved history only; foreign access returns 404; completed-turn-only 24-hour retention; no automatic resend
Verification: Redis integration and Playwright conversation charter

Title: Capability isolation and controls
Given: Healthy history with unavailable provider, occupied model slot and enough session quota
When: Read/replay history, send new work, exhaust quota, race same/different conversations and lose a lease
Then: History survives provider-only outage; unsafe send blocked; healthy busy vs outage codes differ; stale worker cannot commit or release another permit; unknown model usage remains charged
Verification: Real Redis/PostgreSQL guards and controlled provider tests

Title: SSE contract
Given: A valid turn and saved replay
When: Split network chunks within UTF-8/lines, inspect every event and saturate stream capacity
Then: Contiguous identity/sequence and exact delta equality; no text before commit; replay started/completed only; four slots bounded; a fifth returns 503 without model call
Verification: Real Servlet HTTP transport and parser tests

Title: Interrupted stream and reconciliation
Given: A stream has started, a second has deltas, a third has completed
When: Disconnect at each boundary, corrupt sequence, drop commit acknowledgement and fail post-completion history sync
Then: Incomplete text has no links; authoritative recovery deduplicates; completed answer remains confirmed; no automatic JSON fallback/mock/reconnect; actual permits/writers exit safely
Verification: Fault-injected transport tests and Playwright recovery charter

Title: New and clear conversation
Given: Owned saved history and an active turn in another tab
When: Start new conversation; clear active then idle history; lose cookie and try the old UUID
Then: Quotas unchanged; active clear returns 409; idle clear removes only owned transcript; a new UUID used; cookie loss never transfers retained ownership
Verification: Redis session tests and browser multi-tab charter

Title: Exact requests and references
Given: A dated multi-type fixture and last selection order
When: Ask explicit all available, vague intent, missing-year date, now only small, second stone and new search
Then: Explicit all honored; vague/year ambiguity clarified; inherited constraints correct; ordinals stable; no arbitrary name/ID interpretation or status leak
Verification: Fixed-query interpretation and deterministic execution tests

Title: Semantic evidence and late changes
Given: Fixture with card support, type-only support, contradiction, missing vectors and more than five matches
When: Search mixed wishes, then delete/reserve/change a selected stone before commit
Then: Hard filters precede limits; contradiction veto holds; bounded ranking/counts truthful; partial list not padded; one all-lost refresh maximum; no fabricated individual color
Verification: Controlled semantic integration and real-model qualification

Title: Knowledge grounding and attribution
Given: Versioned factual and fictional passages including the source qualification
When: Ask care, personality, ritual and a mixed selection question; open Sources
Then: Fiction explicitly labelled; individual claims supported; same-version citations resolve; no secret keys/scores; missing evidence acknowledged; deleted projection does not break retained citations
Verification: Source parsing, independent answer rubric and browser disclosure checks

Title: Model bounds and valid fallback
Given: A checked selection and a knowledge-only turn under constrained budget/time
When: Force malformed output, late provider failure, limit exhaustion and unknown usage
Then: Counters never reset; current input not truncated; only checked selection may template; knowledge failure remains error; no partial pair or unsafe late commit; reservations settle only reliable usage
Verification: Controlled model/ledger tests and fixed-set assessment

Title: Atomic document replacement
Given: An indexed source and a new version with removed topics
When: Import valid/oversized/malformed sources, fail embedding/commit acknowledgement, replay key after source overwrite and delete projection
Then: Old projection survives confirmed preparation failure; no partial publication; replay does not read/republish the new source; source versions/citations retained; forbidden paths never supplied
Verification: MinIO/pgvector integration and operation-recovery tests

Title: Atomic business event and publisher
Given: A stone mutation with injected outbox failure and a broker outage
When: Commit and roll back changes, reuse an event UUID with a changed payload, recover the broker and fail an event-specific route
Then: Business and outbox changes are atomic; changed payload is rejected; outage preserves the attempt budget; three event-specific failures lead to durable DLQ transfer; acknowledgement alone marks delivery; duplicate deliveries remain permitted
Verification: PostgreSQL/Kafka integration tests

Title: Consumer restart and tombstones
Given: A version 2 deletion, an older update, a malformed record and a failed embedding
When: Redeliver, reorder and restart processing; simulate dependency loss and occupied model capacity
Then: No deleted projection is resurrected; stale versions invoke no model; attempt counts survive restart; dependency outages wait; source offsets advance only after database commit or acknowledged DLQ transfer
Verification: Kafka consumer integration and fault cases

Title: End to end reindex
Given: Existing stones, an orphan projection and one active ALL job
When: Create, update and delete stones during the job; restart; hold Kafka unavailable; supersede a target version and dead-letter one item
Then: Creation remains available; high-water-mark scope is finite; resume does not repeat completed items; ENQUEUED is not DONE; counts lead to SUCCEEDED or COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS with item evidence
Verification: Reindex job integration and operator status inspection

Title: Generated contracts and security
Given: Generated OpenAPI JSON and YAML and every operation in section 10
When: Compare schemas, headers, errors, roles, CSRF, Origin checks, ETags, session expiry and secret redaction
Then: Both formats are equivalent; all operations are documented; there is no competing handwritten contract; authorization and expiry are enforced; no secret or spoofed forwarded-IP identity is accepted
Verification: Generated-contract and security boundary tests

Title: Service objectives and restoration
Given: Declared reference hardware and the specified isolated load fixture
When: Run the stated read, write and indexing samples and restore a catalog/object backup into a new environment
Then: Targets are met or the gate fails with measurements; model timing is not reported as non-model latency; restored catalog and images agree; logs contain no contacts or secrets
Verification: Bounded load qualification and disaster-recovery exercise

Title: Static and architectural handoff
Given: A patch with known positive and negative DTO, layer and style fixtures
When: Invoke the developer wrapper with valid code, a known violation, a missing report and an unapproved suppression
Then: Reports bind to exact content; violations or missing reports block handoff; semantic policies are not falsely claimed as PMD coverage; all relevant pins are verified
Verification: Deterministic wrapper self-tests and architecture fixtures

Title: Environment loss during integration
Given: A requested batch with declared components and isolated endpoints
When: Stop a required database, API or browser dependency between precheck and completion; change content after a passing run
Then: The batch starts only after every prerequisite passes; the watcher detects loss and marks BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT; changed content invalidates evidence; original application data is untouched
Verification: Readiness wrapper failure injection

Title: Swarm to final gate
Given: Matching developer, test and browser evidence with independent reviews
When: Evaluate all-pass, review-rejected, browser-not-run, Sonar-failed, stale-content and mock-only cases
Then: Only all required passes for the same content allow DONE; every other case blocks with a concrete reason; no board connector exists; browser-agent execution is not labelled human testing
Verification: Deterministic gate decision matrix and evidence review

Title: Independent AI qualification
Given: A versioned 20-scenario, 28-turn fixture with source-attribution, fiction and broad-search oracles
When: Collect original real-model results and controlled races under the declared quota
Then: All hard checks, at least 8/9 semantic and 10/12 ordinary-answer scenarios must pass; incomplete cases cannot pass; templates do not inflate quality
Verification: Fixed-set harness and independent acceptance review
